cond_0001.intro: We are looking for an Associate Machinist to join our team. The Associate Machinist reports to the manufacturing supervisor and is responsible for setting up, operating, and maintaining a limited number of machine types in an industrial setting. The position works under a high level of supervision, with limited troubleshooting, decision-making, and problem solving.
cond_0001.responsibilities: Operate machines with little supervision and performs required process checks or inspections per the process documentation. Document non-conforming material according to procedures participate in activities to implement root cause and corrective actions identified. Adhere to all safety standards, regulations and operating procedures. Utilize computer programs to enter part data (e.g., serial number), log time, look up instructions and blueprints and download programs. Utilize work instructions and method documents to produce and inspect machines parts. Utilize various gauging equipment to ensure conformance to the engineering specifications and standards through the production run. Clean and maintain measuring instruments and test equipment and inspects parts for cleanliness (e.g., routed and deburring operations). Operates inspection equipment. Interpret and follow blueprints for proper production task completion. Perform routed operations of parts. Complete paperwork while adhering to record retention requirements. Utilize basic Six Sigma tools and methodology. Communicate information to others about project status, updates, specific instructions, etc and review item status in MRP to ensure item is logged/closed out appropriately. Clean and organize the immediate work area. May perform secondary work functions such as deburring and sub assembly with certifications, as required. Notify supervisors and other personnel of production or machine problems. Promote teamwork within the organization. Verify the calibration of equipment and expiration dates. Complete and review product paperwork, verifying all paperwork is present and filled out appropriately. Follow all departmental safety rules and regulations.
cond_0001.requirements:
Minimum Requirements
High school diploma or equivalent.
Ability to read and use micrometers, functional and cylindrical gauges, comparators, indicator setups, calibration stickers and scales.
Ability to read, interpret, and use drawings, diagrams, and blueprints to determine appropriate activities, tools, and next steps in the production process.
Knowledge of Geometric Dimensioning and Tolerancing such as perpendicularity, parallelism, flatness, including the ability to interpret tolerances on prints, datum structures, material condition tolerances, and orientation tolerances.
Ability to learn non-conformance procedures and processes when parts fail inspection, including knowledge of systems required to log and track failed inspections and associated documentation.
Ability to use computer and web-based systems to input, access, modify, or output information or to execute programs.
Ability to perform simple arithmetic computations including addition, subtraction, multiplication, and division correctly using whole numbers, fractions, decimals, and percentages.
Ability to see details (e.g., letters, numbers, codes, color, symbols, marks, labels, signs) clearly to accomplish work tasks in a safe and efficient manner, with strong hand-eye coordination.
Ability to define, diagnose, and resolve problems with limited troubleshooting and problem solving.
Ability to write effectively, read and understand work documents, communicate information clearly to coworkers and supervisors, and listen attentively and comprehend key pieces of spoken information.
Preferred Requirements
Knowledge of and ability to apply inspection techniques (e.g., formalized inspection standards, inspection instructions, best practices) and use inspection tools efficiently.
Knowledge of part special handling guidelines and specifications.
Ability to read, understand, and edit basic programs and/or basic knowledge of one or more of the following: grinding, turning, milling, drilling.
General knowledge of machines and equipment functionality, and how tools could be used on such equipment/machines, including the ability to learn new systems quickly and understand how parts relate and impact system functionality.
Knowledge of how quality impacts the success of the organization, including costs to customers, costs of recalls, and potential costs due to negative impacts on reputation; includes taking steps to ensure quality consistently and striving for improvement.
Ability to learn and use available business software as necessary.
Ability to accurately provide the information requested on specific forms, reports, and logs.
Ability and willingness to demonstrate eagerness, enthusiasm, and optimism for work activities, including taking ownership of work activities and learning company policies and procedures.
Ability to provide excellent service to internal customers.
No related work experience required.
cond_0001.encouragement_text: Important: Even if you do not meet all of the qualifications and skills listed in the job description, we encourage candidates to apply.
cond_0001.values: We value work that supports people well and reflects genuine care in how it is done. We believe responsibility and respect matter as much as the end result.

cond_0065.intro:
We are looking for someone to join our team in this role.
We are currently looking for Associate Machinists. The Associate Machinist reports to the manufacturing supervisor and is responsible for setting up, operating, and maintaining a limited number of machine types in an industrial setting. The position works under a high level of supervision, with limited troubleshooting, decision-making, and problem solving.
cond_0065.responsibilities: Operate machines with little supervision and performs required process checks or inspections per the process documentation. Document non-conforming material according to procedures participate in activities to implement root cause and corrective actions identified. Adhere to all safety standards, regulations and operating procedures. Utilize computer programs to enter part data (e.g., serial number), log time, look up instructions and blueprints and download programs. Utilize work instructions and method documents to produce and inspect machines parts. Utilize various gauging equipment to ensure conformance to the engineering specifications and standards through the production run. Clean and maintain measuring instruments and test equipment and inspects parts for cleanliness (e.g., routed and deburring operations). Operates inspection equipment. Interpret and follow blueprints for proper production task completion. Perform routed operations of parts. Complete paperwork while adhering to record retention requirements. Utilize basic Six Sigma tools and methodology. Communicate information to others about project status, updates, specific instructions, etc and review item status in MRP to ensure item is logged/closed out appropriately. Clean and organize the immediate work area. May perform secondary work functions such as deburring and sub assembly with certifications, as required. Notify supervisors and other personnel of production or machine problems. Promote teamwork within the organization. Verify the calibration of equipment and expiration dates. Complete and review product paperwork, verifying all paperwork is present and filled out appropriately. Follow all departmental safety rules and regulations.
cond_0065.requirements:
Deep knowledge of and ability to apply inspection techniques (e.g., formalized inspection standards, inspection instructions, best practices) and strong command of inspection tools. Proficiency in reading and using micrometers, functional and cylindrical gauges, comparators, indicator setups, calibration stickers and scales. Solid understanding of how to read, interpret, and use information presented in drawings, diagrams, and blueprints to determine appropriate activities, tools, and next steps in the production process. Ability to learn and use available business software as necessary. Advanced knowledge of part special handling guidelines and specifications. Solid understanding of non-conformance procedures and processes when parts fail inspection, including expertise in systems required to log and track failed inspections and associated documentation as needed within area of responsibility. Advanced knowledge of Geometric Dimensioning and Tolerancing such as perpendicularity, parallelism, and flatness, including the ability to interpret tolerances on prints and perform inspection techniques, interpret datum structures, material condition tolerances, and orientation tolerances. Proficiency in reading, understanding, and editing basic programs and/or solid understanding of one or more of the following: grinding, turning, milling, drilling. Advanced knowledge of how quality impacts the success of the organization including costs to customers, costs of recalls, and potential costs due to negative impacts on reputation, including consistently taking the necessary steps to ensure quality and striving for improvement. Strong command of computer and web-based systems to input, access, modify, or output information or to execute programs. Exceptional written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to read and understand work documents, communicate information clearly to coworkers and supervisors, and listen attentively and comprehend key pieces of spoken information. Solid understanding of machine and equipment functionality and how tools are used on such equipment, including the ability to learn new systems, understand how parts relate, and how they impact system functionality. Ability to provide excellent service to internal customers. Strong ownership of work activities, with the ability and willingness to learn and understand company policies and procedures. Ability to accurately provide information requested on specific forms, reports, and logs. Ability to define, diagnose, and resolve problems with limited troubleshooting and problem solving. Proficiency in performing simple arithmetic computations including addition, subtraction, multiplication, and division using whole numbers, fractions, decimals, and percentages. Strong attention to visual detail (e.g., letters, numbers, codes, color, symbols, marks, labels, signs) and solid hand-eye coordination to accomplish work tasks safely and efficiently. High school diploma or equivalent required. No related work experience required.
Materials and Equipment Used
Machining, hand tools. Nitric and Hydrochloric Acids may be used in certain areas.
Working Environment/ Physical Activities
Moderate physical activity requiring agility and dexterity, including walking, standing, or bending; and lifting or moving objects. Work is performed in an area with moderate risk or discomfort that may require special safety precautions, such as wearing protective clothing or gear.

The Associate Machinist reports to the manufacturing supervisor and is responsible for setting up, operating, and maintaining a limited number of machine types in an industrial setting. The position works under a high level of supervision, with limited troubleshooting, decision-making, and problem solving. A large part of the role involves staying in regular contact with supervisors and coworkers to share updates, flag issues, and keep production running smoothly.
cond_0078.responsibilities:
Operate machines and perform required process checks or inspections per process documentation.
Document non-conforming material according to procedures and actively participate in activities to implement root cause and corrective actions.
Adhere to all safety standards, regulations, and operating procedures.
Utilize computer programs to enter part data (e.g., serial number), log time, look up instructions and blueprints, and download programs.
Utilize work instructions and method documents to produce and inspect machine parts.
Utilize various gauging equipment to ensure conformance to engineering specifications and standards throughout the production run.
Clean and maintain measuring instruments and test equipment; inspect parts for cleanliness (e.g., routed and deburring operations).
Operate inspection equipment.
Interpret and follow blueprints for proper production task completion.
Perform routed operations of parts.
Complete paperwork while adhering to record retention requirements.
Utilize basic Six Sigma tools and methodology.
Regularly communicate information to coworkers and supervisors about project status, updates, and specific instructions; review item status in MRP to ensure items are logged and closed out appropriately.
Clean and organize the immediate work area.
May perform secondary work functions such as deburring and sub-assembly with certifications, as required.
Speak up promptly to notify supervisors and other personnel of production or machine problems.
Promote teamwork within the organization.
Verify the calibration of equipment and expiration dates.
Complete and review product paperwork, verifying all paperwork is present and filled out appropriately.
Follow all departmental safety rules and regulations.
cond_0078.requirements:
Minimum Requirements
High school diploma or equivalent.
Ability to read and use micrometers, functional and cylindrical gauges, comparators, indicator setups, calibration stickers, and scales.
Ability to read, interpret, and use drawings, diagrams, and blueprints to determine appropriate activities, tools, and next steps.
Knowledge of Geometric Dimensioning and Tolerancing (e.g., perpendicularity, parallelism, flatness), including interpreting tolerances, datum structures, material condition tolerances, and orientation tolerances on prints.
Ability to learn and apply inspection techniques using inspection tools efficiently.
Ability to learn non-conformance procedures and processes when parts fail inspection, including systems to log and track failed inspections and documentation.
Ability to use computer and web-based systems to input, access, modify, or output information or execute programs.
Ability to write clearly, read and understand work documents, communicate information to coworkers and supervisors, and listen attentively to spoken information.
Ability to perform simple arithmetic including addition, subtraction, multiplication, and division using whole numbers, fractions, decimals, and percentages.
Ability to see details (e.g., letters, numbers, codes, color, symbols, marks, labels, signs) clearly and possess strong hand-eye coordination.
Ability to define, diagnose, and resolve problems with limited troubleshooting.
No related work experience required.
Preferred Requirements
Basic ability to read, understand, and edit programs; or basic knowledge of one or more of the following: grinding, turning, milling, drilling.
Knowledge of part special handling guidelines and specifications.
General knowledge of machine and equipment functionality, including how parts relate and impact system functionality.
Knowledge of how quality impacts the organization, including costs to customers and costs of recalls; commitment to consistent quality and improvement.
Knowledge of business software relevant to the role.
Ability to accurately complete specific forms, reports, and logs.
Willingness to take ownership of work activities and learn company policies and procedures.
Ability to provide good service to internal customers.
cond_0078.encouragement_text: Important: Even if you do not meet all of the qualifications and skills listed in the job description, we encourage candidates to apply.
cond_0078.values: We value work that supports people well and reflects genuine care in how it is done. We believe responsibility and respect matter as much as the end result.

We are currently looking for Associate Machinists. The Associate Machinist reports to the manufacturing supervisor and is responsible for setting up, operating, and maintaining a limited number of machine types in an industrial setting. The position works under a high level of supervision, with limited troubleshooting, decision-making, and problem solving.
cond_0119.responsibilities: Operate machines with little supervision and performs required process checks or inspections per the process documentation. Document non-conforming material according to procedures participate in activities to implement root cause and corrective actions identified. Adhere to all safety standards, regulations and operating procedures. Utilize computer programs to enter part data (e.g., serial number), log time, look up instructions and blueprints and download programs. Utilize work instructions and method documents to produce and inspect machines parts. Utilize various gauging equipment to ensure conformance to the engineering specifications and standards through the production run. Clean and maintain measuring instruments and test equipment and inspects parts for cleanliness (e.g., routed and deburring operations). Operates inspection equipment. Interpret and follow blueprints for proper production task completion. Perform routed operations of parts. Complete paperwork while adhering to record retention requirements. Utilize basic Six Sigma tools and methodology. Communicate information to others about project status, updates, specific instructions, etc and review item status in MRP to ensure item is logged/closed out appropriately. Clean and organize the immediate work area. May perform secondary work functions such as deburring and sub assembly with certifications, as required. Notify supervisors and other personnel of production or machine problems. Promote teamwork within the organization. Verify the calibration of equipment and expiration dates. Complete and review product paperwork, verifying all paperwork is present and filled out appropriately. Follow all departmental safety rules and regulations.
cond_0119.requirements:
Deep knowledge of and ability to apply inspection techniques (e.g., formalized inspection standards, inspection instructions, best practices) and strong command of inspection tools. Proficiency in reading and using micrometers, functional and cylindrical gauges, comparators, indicator setups, calibration stickers and scales. Solid understanding of how to read, interpret, and use information presented in drawings, diagrams, and blueprints to determine appropriate activities, tools, and next steps in the production process. Ability to learn and use available business software as necessary. Advanced knowledge of part special handling guidelines and specifications. Solid understanding of non-conformance procedures and processes when parts fail inspection, including expertise in systems required to log and track failed inspections and associated documentation as needed within area of responsibility. Advanced knowledge of Geometric Dimensioning and Tolerancing such as perpendicularity, parallelism, and flatness, including the ability to interpret tolerances on prints and perform inspection techniques, interpret datum structures, material condition tolerances, and orientation tolerances. Proficiency in reading, understanding, and editing basic programs and/or solid understanding of one or more of the following: grinding, turning, milling, drilling. Advanced knowledge of how quality impacts the success of the organization including costs to customers, costs of recalls, and potential costs due to negative impacts on reputation, including consistently taking the necessary steps to ensure quality and striving for improvement. Strong command of computer and web-based systems to input, access, modify, or output information or to execute programs. Exceptional written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to read and understand work documents, communicate information clearly to coworkers and supervisors, and listen attentively and comprehend key pieces of spoken information. Solid understanding of machine and equipment functionality and how tools are used on such equipment, including the ability to learn new systems, understand how parts relate, and how they impact system functionality. Ability to provide excellent service to internal customers. Strong ownership of work activities, with the ability and willingness to learn and understand company policies and procedures. Ability to accurately provide information requested on specific forms, reports, and logs. Ability to define, diagnose, and resolve problems with limited troubleshooting and problem solving. Proficiency in performing simple arithmetic computations including addition, subtraction, multiplication, and division using whole numbers, fractions, decimals, and percentages. Strong attention to visual detail (e.g., letters, numbers, codes, color, symbols, marks, labels, signs) and solid hand-eye coordination to accomplish work tasks safely and efficiently. High school diploma or equivalent required. No related work experience required.
Materials and Equipment Used
Machining, hand tools. Nitric and Hydrochloric Acids may be used in certain areas.
Working Environment/ Physical Activities
Moderate physical activity requiring agility and dexterity, including walking, standing, or bending; and lifting or moving objects. Work is performed in an area with moderate risk or discomfort that may require special safety precautions, such as wearing protective clothing or gear.

cond_0132.intro: We are looking for an Associate Machinist to join our team. The Associate Machinist reports to the manufacturing supervisor and is responsible for setting up, operating, and maintaining a limited number of machine types in an industrial setting. The position works under a high level of supervision, with limited troubleshooting, decision-making, and problem solving. A large part of the role involves staying in regular contact with supervisors and coworkers to share updates, flag issues, and keep production running smoothly.
cond_0132.responsibilities:
Operate machines and perform required process checks or inspections per process documentation.
Document non-conforming material according to procedures and actively participate in activities to implement root cause and corrective actions.
Adhere to all safety standards, regulations, and operating procedures.
Utilize computer programs to enter part data (e.g., serial number), log time, look up instructions and blueprints, and download programs.
Utilize work instructions and method documents to produce and inspect machine parts.
Utilize various gauging equipment to ensure conformance to engineering specifications and standards throughout the production run.
Clean and maintain measuring instruments and test equipment; inspect parts for cleanliness (e.g., routed and deburring operations).
Operate inspection equipment.
Interpret and follow blueprints for proper production task completion.
Perform routed operations of parts.
Complete paperwork while adhering to record retention requirements.
Utilize basic Six Sigma tools and methodology.
Regularly communicate information to coworkers and supervisors about project status, updates, and specific instructions; review item status in MRP to ensure items are logged and closed out appropriately.
Clean and organize the immediate work area.
May perform secondary work functions such as deburring and sub-assembly with certifications, as required.
Speak up promptly to notify supervisors and other personnel of production or machine problems.
Promote teamwork within the organization.
Verify the calibration of equipment and expiration dates.
Complete and review product paperwork, verifying all paperwork is present and filled out appropriately.
Follow all departmental safety rules and regulations.
cond_0132.requirements:
Minimum Requirements
High school diploma or equivalent.
Ability to read and use micrometers, functional and cylindrical gauges, comparators, indicator setups, calibration stickers, and scales.
Ability to read, interpret, and use drawings, diagrams, and blueprints to determine appropriate activities, tools, and next steps.
Knowledge of Geometric Dimensioning and Tolerancing (e.g., perpendicularity, parallelism, flatness), including interpreting tolerances, datum structures, material condition tolerances, and orientation tolerances on prints.
Ability to learn and apply inspection techniques using inspection tools efficiently.
Ability to learn non-conformance procedures and processes when parts fail inspection, including systems to log and track failed inspections and documentation.
Ability to use computer and web-based systems to input, access, modify, or output information or execute programs.
Ability to write clearly, read and understand work documents, communicate information to coworkers and supervisors, and listen attentively to spoken information.
Ability to perform simple arithmetic including addition, subtraction, multiplication, and division using whole numbers, fractions, decimals, and percentages.
Ability to see details (e.g., letters, numbers, codes, color, symbols, marks, labels, signs) clearly and possess strong hand-eye coordination.
Ability to define, diagnose, and resolve problems with limited troubleshooting.
No related work experience required.
Preferred Requirements
Basic ability to read, understand, and edit programs; or basic knowledge of one or more of the following: grinding, turning, milling, drilling.
Knowledge of part special handling guidelines and specifications.
General knowledge of machine and equipment functionality, including how parts relate and impact system functionality.
Knowledge of how quality impacts the organization, including costs to customers and costs of recalls; commitment to consistent quality and improvement.
Knowledge of business software relevant to the role.
Ability to accurately complete specific forms, reports, and logs.
Willingness to take ownership of work activities and learn company policies and procedures.
Ability to provide good service to internal customers.

cond_0178.intro: We are looking for an Associate Machinist to join our team. The Associate Machinist reports to the manufacturing supervisor and is responsible for setting up, operating, and maintaining a limited number of machine types in an industrial setting. The position works under a high level of supervision, with limited troubleshooting, decision-making, and problem solving.
cond_0178.responsibilities:
Operate machines with limited supervision and perform required process checks or inspections per process documentation.
Document non-conforming material according to procedures and participate in activities to implement root cause and corrective actions identified.
Adhere to all safety standards, regulations, and operating procedures.
Utilize computer programs to enter part data (e.g., serial number), log time, look up instructions and blueprints, and download programs.
Utilize work instructions and method documents to produce and inspect machine parts.
Utilize various gauging equipment to ensure conformance to engineering specifications and standards through the production run.
Clean and maintain measuring instruments and test equipment; inspect parts for cleanliness (e.g., routed and deburring operations).
Operate inspection equipment.
Interpret and follow blueprints for proper production task completion.
Perform routed operations of parts.
Complete paperwork while adhering to record retention requirements.
Utilize basic Six Sigma tools and methodology.
Document and pass along information on project status, updates, and specific instructions; review item status in MRP to ensure items are logged and closed out appropriately.
Clean and organize the immediate work area.
May perform secondary work functions such as deburring and sub-assembly with certifications, as required.
Notify supervisors and relevant personnel of production or machine problems.
Support teamwork within the organization.
Verify the calibration of equipment and expiration dates.
Complete and review product paperwork, verifying all paperwork is present and filled out appropriately.
Follow all departmental safety rules and regulations.
cond_0178.requirements:
Knowledge of and ability to apply inspection techniques (e.g., formalized inspection standards, inspection instructions, best practices) and use inspection tools efficiently.
Ability to read and use micrometers, functional and cylindrical gauges, comparators, indicator setups, calibration stickers, and scales.
Ability to read, interpret, and use information presented in drawings, diagrams, and blueprints to determine appropriate activities, tools, and next steps in the production process.
Ability to learn and use available business software as necessary.
Knowledge of part special handling guidelines and specifications.
Ability to learn non-conformance procedures and processes when parts fail inspection, including knowledge of systems required to log and track failed inspections and associated documentation within area of responsibility.
Knowledge of Geometric Dimensioning and Tolerancing such as perpendicularity, parallelism, and flatness, including the ability to interpret tolerances on prints, datum structures, material condition tolerances, and orientation tolerances.
Ability to read, understand, and edit basic programs and/or basic knowledge of one or more of the following: grinding, turning, milling, drilling.
Knowledge of how quality impacts the organization, including costs to customers, costs of recalls, and potential costs due to negative impacts on reputation; includes taking necessary steps to ensure consistent quality and striving for improvement.
Ability to use computer and web-based systems to input, access, modify, or output information or to execute programs.
Strong written communication and clear, direct verbal reporting to coworkers and supervisors; ability to listen attentively and comprehend key pieces of spoken information.
General knowledge of machines and equipment functionality and how tools could be used on such equipment; includes the ability to learn new systems, understand how parts relate, and how they impact system functionality.
Ability to provide accurate service to internal customers.
Willingness to take ownership of work activities and learn company policies and procedures.
Ability to accurately provide information requested on specific forms, reports, and logs.
Ability to define, diagnose, and resolve problems with limited troubleshooting and problem solving.
Ability to perform simple arithmetic computations including addition, subtraction, multiplication, and division using whole numbers, fractions, decimals, and percentages.
Ability to see details (e.g., letters, numbers, codes, color, symbols, marks, labels, signs) clearly to accomplish work tasks safely and efficiently; strong hand-eye coordination.
High school diploma or equivalent required.
No related work experience required.
Materials and equipment used: machining, hand tools. Nitric and hydrochloric acids may be used in certain areas.
Moderate physical activity requiring agility and dexterity, including walking, standing, or bending, and lifting or moving objects. Work is performed in an area with moderate risk or discomfort that may require special safety precautions, such as wearing protective clothing or gear.

cond_0284.intro: We are looking for Associate Machinists to join our team. The Associate Machinist reports to the manufacturing supervisor and is responsible for setting up, operating, and maintaining a limited number of machine types in an industrial setting. The position works under a high level of supervision, with limited troubleshooting, decision-making, and problem solving. Most people become stronger in this kind of machining work over time as they build experience and learn from feedback.
cond_0284.responsibilities:
Operate machines with little supervision and performs required process checks or inspections per the process documentation. Document non-conforming material according to procedures participate in activities to implement root cause and corrective actions identified. Adhere to all safety standards, regulations and operating procedures. Utilize computer programs to enter part data (e.g., serial number), log time, look up instructions and blueprints and download programs. Utilize work instructions and method documents to produce and inspect machines parts. Utilize various gauging equipment to ensure conformance to the engineering specifications and standards through the production run. Clean and maintain measuring instruments and test equipment and inspects parts for cleanliness (e.g., routed and deburring operations). Operates inspection equipment. Interpret and follow blueprints for proper production task completion. Perform routed operations of parts. Complete paperwork while adhering to record retention requirements. Utilize basic Six Sigma tools and methodology. Communicate information to others about project status, updates, specific instructions, etc and review item status in MRP to ensure item is logged/closed out appropriately. Clean and organize the immediate work area. May perform secondary work functions such as deburring and sub assembly with certifications, as required. Notify supervisors and other personnel of production or machine problems. Promote teamwork within the organization. Verify the calibration of equipment and expiration dates. Complete and review product paperwork, verifying all paperwork is present and filled out appropriately. Follow all departmental safety rules and regulations.
Materials and Equipment Used
Machining, hand tools. Nitric and Hydrochloric Acids may be used in certain areas.
Working Environment/ Physical Activities
Moderate physical activity requiring agility and dexterity, including walking, standing, or bending; and lifting or moving objects. Work is performed in an area with moderate risk or discomfort that may require special safety precautions, such as wearing protective clothing or gear.
cond_0284.requirements: Knowledge of and ability to apply inspection techniques (e.g., formalized inspection standards, inspection instructions, best practices) and use inspection tools efficiently. The ability to read and use micrometers, functional and cylindrical gauges, comparators, indicator setups, calibration stickers and scales. The ability to read, interpret and use the information presented in drawings, diagrams and blueprints to determine appropriate activities, tools, and next steps in the production process. Ability to learn and use available business software as necessary. Knowledge of part special handling guidelines and specifications. Ability to learn non-conformance procedures and processes when parts fail inspection. This includes knowledge of systems required to log and track failed inspections and associated documentation as needed within area of responsibility. Knowledge of Geometric Dimensioning and Tolerancing such as perpendicularity, parallelism, flatness. This includes the ability to interpret tolerances on prints and perform inspection techniques. This includes the ability to interpret datum structures, material condition tolerances, orientation tolerances. The ability to read, understand, edit basic programs and/or basic knowledge of one or more of the following skills - grinding, turning, milling, drilling. Knowledge of how quality impacts the success of the organization including costs to customers, costs of recalls and potential costs due to negative impacts on a company's reputation. This includes taking the necessary steps to ensure quality on a consistent basis and striving for improvement. The ability to use computer and web-based systems to input, access, modify, or output information or to execute programs. The ability to write effectively, to read and understand work documents, to communicate information clearly to coworkers and supervisors, and the ability to listen attentively and comprehend key pieces of spoken information. General knowledge of machines and equipment functionality, and how tools could be used on such equipment/machines. This includes the ability to learn new systems quickly, understanding how parts relate, and how they impact system functionality. The ability to provide excellent service to internal customers. The ability and willingness to demonstrate eagerness, enthusiasm, and optimism for work activities. This includes the ability and willingness to take ownership of work activities, to learn and understand company policies and procedures. The ability to accurately provide the information requested on specific forms, reports, and logs. The ability to define, diagnose, and resolve problems with limited troubleshooting and problem solving. The ability to perform simple arithmetic computations including addition, subtraction, multiplication, and division correctly using whole numbers, fractions, decimals, and percentages. The ability to see details (e.g., letters, numbers, codes, color, symbols, marks, labels, signs) clearly to accomplish work tasks in a safe and efficient manner and possessing strong hand-eye coordination. High school diploma or equivalent required. No related work experience required.

cond_0304.intro: We are looking for an Associate Machinist to join our team. The Associate Machinist reports to the manufacturing supervisor and is responsible for setting up, operating, and maintaining a limited number of machine types in an industrial setting. The position works under a high level of supervision, with limited troubleshooting, decision-making, and problem solving.
cond_0304.responsibilities:
Operate machines with limited supervision and perform required process checks or inspections per process documentation.
Document non-conforming material according to procedures and participate in activities to implement root cause and corrective actions identified.
Adhere to all safety standards, regulations, and operating procedures.
Utilize computer programs to enter part data (e.g., serial number), log time, look up instructions and blueprints, and download programs.
Utilize work instructions and method documents to produce and inspect machine parts.
Utilize various gauging equipment to ensure conformance to engineering specifications and standards through the production run.
Clean and maintain measuring instruments and test equipment; inspect parts for cleanliness (e.g., routed and deburring operations).
Operate inspection equipment.
Interpret and follow blueprints for proper production task completion.
Perform routed operations of parts.
Complete paperwork while adhering to record retention requirements.
Utilize basic Six Sigma tools and methodology.
Document and pass along information on project status, updates, and specific instructions; review item status in MRP to ensure items are logged and closed out appropriately.
Clean and organize the immediate work area.
May perform secondary work functions such as deburring and sub-assembly with certifications, as required.
Notify supervisors and relevant personnel of production or machine problems.
Support teamwork within the organization.
Verify the calibration of equipment and expiration dates.
Complete and review product paperwork, verifying all paperwork is present and filled out appropriately.
Follow all departmental safety rules and regulations.
cond_0304.requirements:
Knowledge of and ability to apply inspection techniques (e.g., formalized inspection standards, inspection instructions, best practices) and use inspection tools efficiently.
Ability to read and use micrometers, functional and cylindrical gauges, comparators, indicator setups, calibration stickers, and scales.
Ability to read, interpret, and use information presented in drawings, diagrams, and blueprints to determine appropriate activities, tools, and next steps in the production process.
Ability to learn and use available business software as necessary.
Knowledge of part special handling guidelines and specifications.
Ability to learn non-conformance procedures and processes when parts fail inspection, including knowledge of systems required to log and track failed inspections and associated documentation within area of responsibility.
Knowledge of Geometric Dimensioning and Tolerancing such as perpendicularity, parallelism, and flatness, including the ability to interpret tolerances on prints, datum structures, material condition tolerances, and orientation tolerances.
Ability to read, understand, and edit basic programs and/or basic knowledge of one or more of the following: grinding, turning, milling, drilling.
Knowledge of how quality impacts the organization, including costs to customers, costs of recalls, and potential costs due to negative impacts on reputation; includes taking necessary steps to ensure consistent quality and striving for improvement.
Ability to use computer and web-based systems to input, access, modify, or output information or to execute programs.
Strong written communication and clear, direct verbal reporting to coworkers and supervisors; ability to listen attentively and comprehend key pieces of spoken information.
General knowledge of machines and equipment functionality and how tools could be used on such equipment; includes the ability to learn new systems, understand how parts relate, and how they impact system functionality.
Ability to provide accurate service to internal customers.
Willingness to take ownership of work activities and learn company policies and procedures.
Ability to accurately provide information requested on specific forms, reports, and logs.
Ability to define, diagnose, and resolve problems with limited troubleshooting and problem solving.
Ability to perform simple arithmetic computations including addition, subtraction, multiplication, and division using whole numbers, fractions, decimals, and percentages.
Ability to see details (e.g., letters, numbers, codes, color, symbols, marks, labels, signs) clearly to accomplish work tasks safely and efficiently; strong hand-eye coordination.
High school diploma or equivalent required.
No related work experience required.
Materials and equipment used: machining, hand tools. Nitric and hydrochloric acids may be used in certain areas.
Moderate physical activity requiring agility and dexterity, including walking, standing, or bending, and lifting or moving objects. Work is performed in an area with moderate risk or discomfort that may require special safety precautions, such as wearing protective clothing or gear.

The position works under a high level of supervision, with limited troubleshooting, decision-making, and problem solving. Most people grow into this work over time as they build hands-on experience with machining and production processes.
cond_0311.responsibilities: Operate machines with little supervision and performs required process checks or inspections per the process documentation. Document non-conforming material according to procedures participate in activities to implement root cause and corrective actions identified. Adhere to all safety standards, regulations and operating procedures. Utilize computer programs to enter part data (e.g., serial number), log time, look up instructions and blueprints and download programs. Utilize work instructions and method documents to produce and inspect machines parts. Utilize various gauging equipment to ensure conformance to the engineering specifications and standards through the production run. Clean and maintain measuring instruments and test equipment and inspects parts for cleanliness (e.g., routed and deburring operations). Operates inspection equipment. Interpret and follow blueprints for proper production task completion. Perform routed operations of parts. Complete paperwork while adhering to record retention requirements. Utilize basic Six Sigma tools and methodology. Communicate information to others about project status, updates, specific instructions, etc and review item status in MRP to ensure item is logged/closed out appropriately. Clean and organize the immediate work area. May perform secondary work functions such as deburring and sub assembly with certifications, as required. Notify supervisors and other personnel of production or machine problems. Promote teamwork within the organization. Verify the calibration of equipment and expiration dates. Complete and review product paperwork, verifying all paperwork is present and filled out appropriately. Follow all departmental safety rules and regulations.
cond_0311.requirements:
Minimum Requirements
High school diploma or equivalent
Ability to read and use microchmeters, functional and cylindrical gauges, comparators, indicator setups, calibration stickers and scales
Ability to read, interpret and use information presented in drawings, diagrams and blueprints to determine appropriate activities, tools, and next steps in the production process
Knowledge of and ability to apply inspection techniques (e.g., formalized inspection standards, inspection instructions, best practices) and use inspection tools efficiently
Ability to learn non-conformance procedures and processes when parts fail inspection, including knowledge of systems required to log and track failed inspections and associated documentation
Ability to use computer and web-based systems to input, access, modify, or output information or to execute programs
Ability to learn and use available business software as necessary
Ability to write effectively, read and understand work documents, communicate information clearly to coworkers and supervisors, and listen attentively and comprehend key pieces of spoken information
Ability to perform simple arithmetic computations including addition, subtraction, multiplication, and division correctly using whole numbers, fractions, decimals, and percentages
Ability to see details (e.g., letters, numbers, codes, color, symbols, marks, labels, signs) clearly to accomplish work tasks in a safe and efficient manner, with strong hand-and-eye coordination
Ability to define, diagnose, and resolve problems with limited troubleshooting and problem solving
Ability to accurately provide the information requested on specific forms, reports, and logs
No related work experience required
Preferred Requirements
Knowledge of Geometric Dimensioning and Tolerancing such as perpendicularity, parallelism, and flatness, including the ability to interpret tolerances on prints, datum structures, material condition tolerances, and orientation tolerances
Ability to read, understand, and edit basic programs and/or basic knowledge of one or more of the following: grinding, turning, milling, drilling
Knowledge of part special handling guidelines and specifications
General knowledge of machines and equipment functionality, and how tools could be used on such equipment/machines, including the ability to learn new systems quickly, understand how parts relate, and how they impact system functionality
Knowledge of how quality impacts the success of the organization including costs to customers, costs of recalls and potential costs due to negative impacts on a company's reputation, including taking the necessary steps to ensure quality on a consistent basis and striving for improvement
Ability and willingness to demonstrate eagerness, enthusiasm, and optimism for work activities, including taking ownership of work activities and learning and understanding company policies and procedures
cond_0311.values: We value excellence and take pride in delivering strong results. We aim to hold a high standard in our work and in the outcomes we create.

cond_0312.intro: We are looking for an Associate Machinist to join our team. Speak up promptly to notify supervisors and other personnel of production or machine problems.
Promote teamwork within the organization.

Complete and review product paperwork, verifying all paperwork is present and filled out appropriately.
Follow all departmental safety rules and regulations.

Ability to define, diagnose, and resolve problems with limited troubleshooting.
No related work experience required.

Basic ability to read, understand, and edit programs; or basic knowledge of one or more of the following: grinding, turning, milling, drilling.

cond_0371.intro:
We are looking for someone to join our team in this role.
We are currently looking for Associate Machinists. The Associate Machinist reports to the manufacturing supervisor and is responsible for setting up, operating, and maintaining a limited number of machine types in an industrial setting. The position works under a high level of supervision, with limited troubleshooting, decision-making, and problem solving.
cond_0371.responsibilities: Operate machines with little supervision and performs required process checks or inspections per the process documentation. Document non-conforming material according to procedures participate in activities to implement root cause and corrective actions identified. Adhere to all safety standards, regulations and operating procedures. Utilize computer programs to enter part data (e.g., serial number), log time, look up instructions and blueprints and download programs. Utilize work instructions and method documents to produce and inspect machines parts. Utilize various gauging equipment to ensure conformance to the engineering specifications and standards through the production run. Clean and maintain measuring instruments and test equipment and inspects parts for cleanliness (e.g., routed and deburring operations). Operates inspection equipment. Interpret and follow blueprints for proper production task completion. Perform routed operations of parts. Complete paperwork while adhering to record retention requirements. Utilize basic Six Sigma tools and methodology. Communicate information to others about project status, updates, specific instructions, etc and review item status in MRP to ensure item is logged/closed out appropriately. Clean and organize the immediate work area. May perform secondary work functions such as deburring and sub assembly with certifications, as required. Notify supervisors and other personnel of production or machine problems. Promote teamwork within the organization. Verify the calibration of equipment and expiration dates. Complete and review product paperwork, verifying all paperwork is present and filled out appropriately. Follow all departmental safety rules and regulations.
cond_0371.requirements:
Deep knowledge of and ability to apply inspection techniques (e.g., formalized inspection standards, inspection instructions, best practices) and strong command of inspection tools. Proficiency in reading and using micrometers, functional and cylindrical gauges, comparators, indicator setups, calibration stickers and scales. Solid understanding of how to read, interpret, and use information presented in drawings, diagrams, and blueprints to determine appropriate activities, tools, and next steps in the production process. Ability to learn and use available business software as necessary. Advanced knowledge of part special handling guidelines and specifications. Solid understanding of non-conformance procedures and processes when parts fail inspection, including expertise in systems required to log and track failed inspections and associated documentation as needed within area of responsibility. Advanced knowledge of Geometric Dimensioning and Tolerancing such as perpendicularity, parallelism, and flatness, including the ability to interpret tolerances on prints and perform inspection techniques, interpret datum structures, material condition tolerances, and orientation tolerances. Proficiency in reading, understanding, and editing basic programs and/or solid understanding of one or more of the following: grinding, turning, milling, drilling. Advanced knowledge of how quality impacts the success of the organization including costs to customers, costs of recalls, and potential costs due to negative impacts on reputation, including consistently taking the necessary steps to ensure quality and striving for improvement. Strong command of computer and web-based systems to input, access, modify, or output information or to execute programs. Exceptional written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to read and understand work documents, communicate information clearly to coworkers and supervisors, and listen attentively and comprehend key pieces of spoken information. Solid understanding of machine and equipment functionality and how tools are used on such equipment, including the ability to learn new systems, understand how parts relate, and how they impact system functionality. Ability to provide excellent service to internal customers. Strong ownership of work activities, with the ability and willingness to learn and understand company policies and procedures. Ability to accurately provide information requested on specific forms, reports, and logs. Ability to define, diagnose, and resolve problems with limited troubleshooting and problem solving. Proficiency in performing simple arithmetic computations including addition, subtraction, multiplication, and division using whole numbers, fractions, decimals, and percentages. Strong attention to visual detail (e.g., letters, numbers, codes, color, symbols, marks, labels, signs) and solid hand-eye coordination to accomplish work tasks safely and efficiently. High school diploma or equivalent required. No related work experience required.
Materials and Equipment Used
Machining, hand tools. Nitric and Hydrochloric Acids may be used in certain areas.
Working Environment/ Physical Activities
Moderate physical activity requiring agility and dexterity, including walking, standing, or bending; and lifting or moving objects. Work is performed in an area with moderate risk or discomfort that may require special safety precautions, such as wearing protective clothing or gear.

The position works under a high level of supervision, with limited troubleshooting, decision-making, and problem solving. A large part of the role involves staying in regular contact with supervisors and coworkers to share updates, flag issues, and keep production running smoothly.
cond_0384.responsibilities:
Operate machines and perform required process checks or inspections per process documentation.
Document non-conforming material according to procedures and actively participate in activities to implement root cause and corrective actions.
Adhere to all safety standards, regulations, and operating procedures.
Utilize computer programs to enter part data (e.g., serial number), log time, look up instructions and blueprints, and download programs.
Utilize work instructions and method documents to produce and inspect machine parts.
Utilize various gauging equipment to ensure conformance to engineering specifications and standards throughout the production run.
Clean and maintain measuring instruments and test equipment; inspect parts for cleanliness (e.g., routed and deburring operations).
Operate inspection equipment.
Interpret and follow blueprints for proper production task completion.
Perform routed operations of parts.
Complete paperwork while adhering to record retention requirements.
Utilize basic Six Sigma tools and methodology.
Regularly communicate information to coworkers and supervisors about project status, updates, and specific instructions; review item status in MRP to ensure items are logged and closed out appropriately.
Clean and organize the immediate work area.
May perform secondary work functions such as deburring and sub-assembly with certifications, as required.
Speak up promptly to notify supervisors and other personnel of production or machine problems.
Promote teamwork within the organization.
Verify the calibration of equipment and expiration dates.
Complete and review product paperwork, verifying all paperwork is present and filled out appropriately.
Follow all departmental safety rules and regulations.
cond_0384.requirements:
Minimum Requirements
High school diploma or equivalent.
Ability to read and use micrometers, functional and cylindrical gauges, comparators, indicator setups, calibration stickers, and scales.
Ability to read, interpret, and use drawings, diagrams, and blueprints to determine appropriate activities, tools, and next steps.
Knowledge of Geometric Dimensioning and Tolerancing (e.g., perpendicularity, parallelism, flatness), including interpreting tolerances, datum structures, material condition tolerances, and orientation tolerances on prints.
Ability to learn and apply inspection techniques using inspection tools efficiently.
Ability to learn non-conformance procedures and processes when parts fail inspection, including systems to log and track failed inspections and documentation.
Ability to use computer and web-based systems to input, access, modify, or output information or execute programs.
Ability to write clearly, read and understand work documents, communicate information to coworkers and supervisors, and listen attentively to spoken information.
Ability to perform simple arithmetic including addition, subtraction, multiplication, and division using whole numbers, fractions, decimals, and percentages.
Ability to see details (e.g., letters, numbers, codes, color, symbols, marks, labels, signs) clearly and possess strong hand-eye coordination.
Ability to define, diagnose, and resolve problems with limited troubleshooting.
No related work experience required.
Preferred Requirements
Basic ability to read, understand, and edit programs; or basic knowledge of one or more of the following: grinding, turning, milling, drilling.
Knowledge of part special handling guidelines and specifications.
General knowledge of machine and equipment functionality, including how parts relate and impact system functionality.
Knowledge of how quality impacts the organization, including costs to customers and costs of recalls; commitment to consistent quality and improvement.
Knowledge of business software relevant to the role.
Ability to accurately complete specific forms, reports, and logs.
Willingness to take ownership of work activities and learn company policies and procedures.
Ability to provide good service to internal customers.
cond_0384.values: We value excellence and take pride in delivering strong results. We aim to hold a high standard in our work and in the outcomes we create.
cond_0384.inclusion: We actively seek women candidates with a wide range of perspectives and backgrounds, and we are proud to be an equal opportunity employer. The ability to read and use micrometers, functional and cylindrical gauges, comparators, indicator setups, calibration stickers and scales, or a willingness to learn these tools. The ability to read, interpret and use the information presented in drawings, diagrams and blueprints to determine appropriate activities, tools, and next steps in the production process. Willingness to learn and use available business software as necessary. Some exposure to part special handling guidelines and specifications is helpful. Willingness to learn non-conformance procedures and processes when parts fail inspection, including systems used to log and track failed inspections and associated documentation within area of responsibility. Background in or openness to learning Geometric Dimensioning and Tolerancing such as perpendicularity, parallelism, flatness, including interpreting tolerances on prints, datum structures, material condition tolerances, and orientation tolerances. The ability to read, understand, and edit basic programs and/or working knowledge of one or more of the following — grinding, turning, milling, drilling. Some understanding of how quality impacts the success of the organization, including costs to customers and the importance of consistent quality; a willingness to take steps to ensure quality and strive for improvement. The ability to use computer and web-based systems to input, access, modify, or output information or to execute programs. The ability to write effectively, to read and understand work documents, to communicate information clearly to coworkers and supervisors, and the ability to listen attentively and comprehend key pieces of spoken information. General familiarity with machines and equipment functionality, and how tools could be used on such equipment; a willingness to learn new systems and understand how parts relate and impact system functionality. The ability to provide good service to internal customers. A willingness to take ownership of work activities and learn company policies and procedures. The ability to accurately provide the information requested on specific forms, reports, and logs. The ability to define, diagnose, and resolve problems with limited troubleshooting and problem solving. The ability to perform simple arithmetic computations including addition, subtraction, multiplication, and division correctly using whole numbers, fractions, decimals, and percentages. The ability to see details (e.g., letters, numbers, codes, color, symbols, marks, labels, signs) clearly to accomplish work tasks in a safe and efficient manner and possessing adequate hand-eye coordination. High school diploma or equivalent required, or equivalent practical experience. No related work experience required.
Materials and Equipment Used
Machining, hand tools. Nitric and Hydrochloric Acids may be used in certain areas.
Working Environment/ Physical Activities
Moderate physical activity requiring agility and dexterity, including walking, standing, or bending; and lifting or moving objects. Work is performed in an area with moderate risk or discomfort that may require special safety precautions, such as wearing protective clothing or gear.
cond_0426.values: We value excellence and take pride in delivering strong results. We aim to hold a high standard in our work and in the outcomes we create.

cond_0427.intro: We are looking for Associate Machinists to join our team. Document non-conforming material according to procedures and take ownership of activities to implement root cause and corrective actions identified.
Adhere to all safety standards, regulations, and operating procedures.
Utilize computer programs to enter part data (e.g., serial number), log time, look up instructions and blueprints, and download programs.
Apply work instructions and method documents to produce and inspect machine parts.
Use various gauging equipment to ensure conformance to engineering specifications and standards throughout the production run.
Clean and maintain measuring instruments and test equipment; inspect parts for cleanliness (e.g., routed and deburring operations).
Operate inspection equipment.
Interpret and follow blueprints to direct proper production task completion.
Perform routed operations of parts.
Complete paperwork while adhering to record retention requirements.
Apply basic Six Sigma tools and methodology.
Deliver clear communication to others about project status, updates, and specific instructions; review item status in MRP to ensure items are logged and closed out appropriately.
Clean and organize the immediate work area.
May perform secondary work functions such as deburring and sub assembly with certifications, as required.
Identify and report production or machine problems to supervisors and other personnel.
Promote teamwork within the organization.
Verify the calibration of equipment and expiration dates.
Complete and review product paperwork, ensuring all paperwork is present and filled out appropriately.
Follow all departmental safety rules and regulations.
cond_0548.requirements:
Minimum Requirements
Knowledge of and ability to apply inspection techniques (e.g., formalized inspection standards, inspection instructions, best practices) and use inspection tools efficiently.
Ability to read and use micrometers, functional and cylindrical gauges, comparators, indicator setups, calibration stickers, and scales.
Ability to read, interpret, and use information presented in drawings, diagrams, and blueprints to determine appropriate activities, tools, and next steps in the production process.
Ability to learn non-conformance procedures and processes when parts fail inspection, including knowledge of systems to log and track failed inspections and associated documentation.
Ability to use computer and web-based systems to input, access, modify, or output information or to execute programs.
Ability to write effectively, read and understand work documents, communicate information clearly to coworkers and supervisors, and listen attentively to comprehend key pieces of spoken information.
Ability to define, diagnose, and resolve problems with limited troubleshooting and problem solving.
Ability to perform simple arithmetic computations including addition, subtraction, multiplication, and division using whole numbers, fractions, decimals, and percentages.
Ability to see details (e.g., letters, numbers, codes, color, symbols, marks, labels, signs) clearly to accomplish work tasks safely and efficiently, with strong hand-eye coordination.
High school diploma or equivalent.
No related work experience required.
Preferred Requirements
Knowledge of Geometric Dimensioning and Tolerancing such as perpendicularity, parallelism, and flatness, including the ability to interpret tolerances on prints, datum structures, material condition tolerances, and orientation tolerances.
Ability to read, understand, and edit basic programs and/or basic knowledge of one or more of the following: grinding, turning, milling, drilling.
Knowledge of part special handling guidelines and specifications.
Knowledge of how quality impacts the organization, including costs to customers, costs of recalls, and potential reputational costs; includes taking steps to ensure consistent quality and striving for improvement.
General knowledge of machines and equipment functionality and how tools could be used on such equipment, including the ability to learn new systems quickly and understand how parts relate and impact system functionality.
Ability to learn and use available business software as necessary.
Ability to accurately provide information requested on specific forms, reports, and logs.
Ability and willingness to demonstrate eagerness, enthusiasm, and optimism for work activities, including taking ownership of work activities and learning company policies and procedures.
Materials and Equipment Used
Machining, hand tools. Nitric and Hydrochloric Acids may be used in certain areas.
Working Environment/ Physical Activities
Moderate physical activity requiring agility and dexterity, including walking, standing, or bending; and lifting or moving objects. Work is performed in an area with moderate risk or discomfort that may require special safety precautions, such as wearing protective clothing or gear.

High school diploma or equivalent
Ability to read and use micrometers, functional and cylindrical gauges, comparators, indicator setups, calibration stickers and scales

Ability to write effectively, read and understand work documents, communicate information clearly to coworkers and supervisors, and listen attentively and comprehend key pieces of spoken information

Ability to read, understand, and edit basic programs and/or basic knowledge of one or more of the following: grinding, turning, milling, drilling
